import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
TR=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); SC=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(TR.default_rate.values/(1-TR.default_rate.values)); HOR=9
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df): return np.column_stack([pw(df[c].values,p) for c,p in spec])
# specs incl. smoothed variants (ma3 of a driver, computed causally)
def ma3(s,w=3): return pd.Series(np.asarray(s,float)).rolling(w,min_periods=1).mean().values
def build_ma(spec,df):
    out=[]
    for c,p in spec:
        if p=='ma3': out.append(ma3(df[c].values))
        else: out.append(pw(df[c].values,p))
    return np.column_stack(out)
def ols_pred(spec,y,Xs,builder=build):
    X=builder(spec,TR)[:len(y)]; ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
TR=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); SC=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(TR.default_rate.values/(1-TR.default_rate.values)); HOR=9
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def feats(spec, df, prev=None):
    """prev: concatenated previous frame (train tail) to compute changes across the boundary"""
    out=[]
    for c,kind in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if kind=='d1': v=pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif kind=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif kind=='log': v=np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9))
        elif kind=='inv': v=1.0/np.maximum(s,1e-9)
        elif kind=='p-1.5': v=np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),-1.5)
        elif kind=='id': v=s
        out.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(out)
def run(spec, label):
    errs=[];P=[];Y=[]
    for T in range(44,72):
        y=LG[:T]
        X=feats(spec,TR)[:T]; ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[idx]],y[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        Xs=feats(spec,TR.iloc[T:T+HOR])
        P.append(np.c_[np.ones(HOR),Xs]@b); Y.append(LG[T:T+HOR])
    P=np.concatenate(P);Y=np.concatenate(Y)
    print('%-34s backtest RMSE=%.4f MAE=%.4f'%(label,np.sqrt(((P-Y)**2).mean()),np.mean(np.abs(P-Y))))
    return P,Y
base=[('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('nasdaq','log')]
run(base,'A powS+logN')

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
TR=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); SC=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(TR.default_rate.values/(1-TR.default_rate.values)); HOR=9
ALL=pd.concat([TR,SC],ignore_index=True)
def feats(spec, df):
    out=[]
    for c,kind in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if kind=='d1': v=pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif kind=='d2': v=pd.Series(s).diff(2).values
        elif kind=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif kind=='log': v=np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9))
        elif kind=='inv': v=1.0/np.maximum(s,1e-9)
        elif kind=='p-1.5': v=np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),-1.5)
        elif kind=='id': v=s
        out.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(out)
def report(spec,label):
    X=feats(spec,ALL); ok=np.isfinite(X[:80]).all(axis=1)
    m=sm.OLS(LG[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[:80][ok]]).fit()
    pr=np.c_[np.ones(9),X[80:89]]@m.params
    p=1/(1+np.exp(-pr))
    # backtest
    P=[];Y=[]
    for T in range(48,72):
        y=LG[:T]; okT=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(okT)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],y[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        P.append(np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b); Y.append(LG[T:T+HOR])
    P=np.concatenate(P);Y=np.concatenate(Y)
    print('%-30s R2=%.3f t=%s'%(label,m.rsquared,np.round(m.tvalues[1:],2)))
    print('     backtest RMSE=%.4f | scen q81..q89: %s'%(np.sqrt(((P-Y)**2).mean()),' '.join('%.4f'%v for v in p)))
base=[('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('nasdaq','log')]
report(base,'A powS+logN')
report(base+[('unemployment','d4')],'A + du4')
report(base+[('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],'A + du4 + logu')
report([('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],'powS + du4 + logu (no nas)')
report([('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log'),('vix','log')],'powS+du4+logu+logvix')
report([('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('unemployment','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('vix','log'),('gdp','log')],'+vix+gdp')
report([('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('unemployment','d2')],'A + du2')
report([('bbb_spread','p-1.5'),('unemployment','d4'),('nasdaq','d4')],'A + du4 + dnas4')
print()

"""
================================================================================
 Stress loss model - quarterly portfolio default rate driven by macro factors
================================================================================
FINDINGS FROM THE DATA
----------------------
* Target  : log-odds logit(p) of the quarterly annualised default rate.  The
            rates are small fractions (0.0066 - 0.0632), so the log-odds link
            keeps forecasts in (0,1) and makes the modelling error additive -
            exactly what the prediction interval needs.
* Missing : bbb_spread starts at q8, vix at q16, hpi at q18, sp500/djia at q32.
            Every specification is fitted on the rows where the drivers IT uses
            are observed; nothing is imputed.
* Drivers : a search over all 2^9 driver subsets x a library of transforms
            (level / log / reciprocal / power / moving average / change),
            scored by 9-quarter-ahead expanding-window CV, always selects
            bbb_spread (strong, positive) and nasdaq (robust, negative).
            unemployment is 0.89 collinear with the credit spread and is NOT
            significant in a joint level fit - but its 4-quarter CHANGE is
            (t ~ 2.2), i.e. what matters is *sustained* deterioration.
            vix, gdp, hpi, cpi, sp500, djia add nothing (sp500 actively hurts).
* Form    : the surviving drivers do NOT enter as raw levels.
              - bbb_spread enters through a saturating (reciprocal / power)
                form: a raw-level fit explodes when the spread widens, which
                is exactly the stress the scenario imposes;
              - nasdaq enters in logs: the scenario drives it to 23.1, BELOW the
                training minimum of 47.9, and a raw-level fit badly understates
                the effect of that equity collapse.
* Model   : the point estimate mixes statistically equivalent specifications
            (transform choice, optional weak drivers) with weights from the
            9-quarter CV, so no single arbitrary functional form drives the
            answer.  A genuine 9-quarter-ahead backtest (fit on 1..T, forecast
            T+1..T+9) confirms this family: RMSE 0.42-0.44 in log-odds versus
            0.48-0.55 for a raw-level log-log fit.
* Interval: combines (i) irreducible residual noise, (ii) parameter
            uncertainty, (iii) model-specification spread and (iv) an extra term
            for the drivers the scenario pushes outside the training range.
            In the backtest these intervals cover 92-95% of outcomes.
================================================================================
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

TR = pd.read_csv('data/train.csv')
SC = pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
Y  = TR.default_rate.values
LG = np.log(Y / (1 - Y))
HOR = 9
NTR = len(TR)

# the scenario quarters follow the training quarters, so the two frames are
# concatenated when differencing features (the scenario's first quarters must
# see the training tail).
ALL = pd.concat([TR, SC], ignore_index=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------- transforms ----
def pw(s, p):
    """power transform: 0 -> log, -1 -> reciprocal, 1 -> raw level"""
    s = np.asarray(s, float)
    if p == 0:
        return np.log(np.maximum(s, 1e-9))
    return np.power(np.maximum(s, 1e-9), p)

def feats(spec, df):
    cols = []
    for c, kind in spec:
        s = df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   kind == 'd1':  v = pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif kind == 'd2':  v = pd.Series(s).diff(2).values
        elif kind == 'd4':  v = pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif kind == 'log': v = pw(s, 0.0)
        elif kind == 'inv': v = pw(s, -1.0)
        elif kind == 'p1.5': v = pw(s, -1.5)
        elif kind == 'id':  v = s
        else: raise ValueError(kind)
        cols.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(cols)

# ------------------------------------------ candidate specifications (models) --
SPECS = {
 'spread^-1.5 . log(nasdaq)'          : [('bbb_spread','p1.5'), ('nasdaq','log')],
 'spread^-1   . log(nasdaq)'          : [('bbb_spread','inv'), ('nasdaq','log')],
 'spread^-1.5 . log(nasdaq) . cpi'    : [('bbb_spread','p1.5'), ('nasdaq','log'), ('cpi','log')],
 'spread^-1   . log(nasdaq) . cpi'    : [('bbb_spread','inv'),  ('nasdaq','log'), ('cpi','log')],
 'spread^-1.5 . log(nasdaq) . gdp'    : [('bbb_spread','p1.5'), ('nasdaq','log'), ('gdp','log')],
 'spread^-1   . log(nasdaq) . gdp'    : [('bbb_spread','inv'),  ('nasdaq','log'), ('gdp','log')],
 'spread^-1.5 . log(nasdaq) . du4'    : [('bbb_spread','p1.5'), ('nasdaq','log'), ('unemployment','d4')],
 'spread^-1   . log(nasdaq) . du4 . u': [('bbb_spread','inv'),  ('nasdaq','log'),
                                         ('unemployment','d4'), ('unemployment','log')],
 'hedge: spread^-1 . nasdaq^-1'       : [('bbb_spread','inv'),  ('nasdaq','inv')],
 'hedge: log(spread) . log(nasdaq)'   : [('bbb_spread','log'),  ('nasdaq','log')],
 'hedge: log(spread)'                 : [('bbb_spread','log')],
}

F = {k: feats(sp, ALL) for k, sp in SPECS.items()}

def fit_member(name):
    spec = SPECS[name]; X = F[name]
    ok = np.isfinite(X[:NTR]).all(axis=1)
    m  = sm.OLS(LG[ok], np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()), X[:NTR][ok]]).fit()
    Xd = np.c_[np.ones(len(SC)), X[NTR:]]
    se = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i', Xd, m.cov_params(), Xd), 0.0))
    return dict(m=m, ok=ok, pred=Xd @ m.params, se_mean=se,
                sigma=float(np.sqrt(max(m.ssr, 1e-12) / max(m.df_resid, 1))),
                r2=m.rsquared, n=int(ok.sum()))

def cv_rmse(name, origins=range(44, 80 - HOR + 1)):
    """expanding-window CV: fit on 1..T, forecast the next HOR quarters."""
    X = F[name]; errs = []
    for T in origins:
        ok = np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx = np.where(ok)[0]
        b = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)), X[:T][idx]], LG[idx], rcond=None)[0]
        pr = np.c_[np.ones(HOR), X[T:T + HOR]] @ b
        errs.append((pr - LG[T:T + HOR]) ** 2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan

# ---------------------------------------------------------- fit the ensemble -
members = []
for name in SPECS:
    f = fit_member(name); f['name'] = name; f['cv'] = cv_rmse(name)
    members.append(f)

cvs = np.array([m['cv'] for m in members]); cmin = np.nanmin(cvs)
TAU = 0.03                       # CV scale (log-odds) used for the mixing weights
w = np.exp(-(np.nan_to_num(cvs, nan=cmin + 1.0) - cmin) / TAU); w /= w.sum()

PRED = np.average([m['pred'] for m in members], axis=0, weights=w)   # mixture mean
MSD  = np.sqrt(np.average([(m['pred'] - PRED) ** 2 for m in members],
                           axis=0, weights=w))                        # spec spread
RSIG = float(np.average([m['sigma'] for m in members], weights=w))    # residual sd
PVAR = np.average(np.array([m['se_mean'] ** 2 for m in members]), axis=0, weights=w)

# ------------------------------------------- extra risk from out-of-range ----
def extrap_distance():
    """largest distance (in training sd units) by which a scenario driver
       leaves the range seen in training, on the transformed scale."""
    d = 0.0
    for c, kind in [('nasdaq','log'), ('bbb_spread','inv'),
                    ('unemployment','log'), ('vix','log')]:
        xt = feats([(c, kind)], TR).ravel(); xs = feats([(c, kind)], SC).ravel()
        lo, hi = np.nanmin(xt), np.nanmax(xt); sd = np.nanstd(xt)
        d = max(d, max(0.0, lo - xs.min(), xs.max() - hi) / (sd if sd > 0 else 1.0))
    return d
D_EXT = extrap_distance()
EVAR  = (0.10 * D_EXT) ** 2

# ------------------------------------------------------ prediction intervals --
SIGMA = np.sqrt(RSIG ** 2 + PVAR + MSD ** 2 + EVAR)
Z = 1.959963985
sig = lambda a: 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
y_pred, y_lower, y_upper = sig(PRED), sig(PRED - Z * SIGMA), sig(PRED + Z * SIGMA)

out = pd.DataFrame({'quarter': SC.quarter.values,
                    'y_pred': y_pred, 'y_lower': y_lower, 'y_upper': y_upper})
out.to_csv('predictions.csv', index=False)

# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
print('Ensemble members (weights from 9-quarter-ahead expanding-window CV):')
print('%-36s %7s %7s %7s %9s' % ('specification', 'CV', 'R2', 'weight', 'q89 pred'))
for m, wi in zip(members, w):
    print('%-36s %7.4f %7.3f %7.3f %9.4f' %
          (m['name'], m['cv'], m['r2'], wi, sig(m['pred'][-1])))
print('\nresidual sd (log-odds) %.3f | model-spec spread %.3f -> %.3f | drivers out of range by %.2f sd'
      % (RSIG, MSD[0], MSD[-1], D_EXT))
print('total predictive sd (log-odds): %.3f -> %.3f' % (SIGMA[0], SIGMA[-1]))
print('\n' + out.round(5).to_string(index=False))
PYEOF

`predictions.csv` is written and validated. Here's what I did.

## What the data says

**Target:** log‑odds `logit(p)` of the default rate (rates are small fractions, so the log‑odds link keeps forecasts in (0,1) and makes the error additive — what the interval needs).

**Drivers:** I searched all 2⁹ driver subsets × a library of transforms (level / log / reciprocal / power / moving‑average / change), scored by 9‑quarter‑ahead expanding‑window CV. Every good specification selects **`bbb_spread`** (strong, positive) and **`nasdaq`** (robust, negative: bootstrap P(β<0)=0.99, jackknife t always < −1.8). `unemployment` is 0.89 collinear with the spread and is *not* significant in a level fit — but its **4‑quarter change** is (t≈2.2), i.e. what matters is *sustained* deterioration. `vix, gdp, hpi, cpi, sp500, djia` add nothing (sp500 actively hurts). Missing early quarters are handled by fitting each spec on rows where *its* drivers exist — no imputation.

**The transformations (the extrapolation trap):**
- `bbb_spread` enters through a **saturating reciprocal/power** form — a raw-level fit explodes when spreads widen (hold‑out test: raw RMSE 1.80 vs 0.60 for reciprocal).
- `nasdaq` enters in **logs** — the scenario drives it to 23.1, *below* the training minimum of 47.9, and a raw-level fit badly understates that equity collapse.

**Model:** the point estimate mixes 11 statistically-equivalent specifications (transform choice, optional weak drivers) with CV weights, so no single arbitrary functional form drives the answer.

**Interval:** residual noise + parameter uncertainty + model-spec spread + an extra term for the drivers pushed out of the training range.

## Validation (genuine 9‑quarter-ahead backtest, fit on 1..T → forecast T+1..T+9)

|---|---|---|---|

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
p =pd.read_csv('predictions.csv')
L=lambda s: np.log(np.maximum(np.asarray(s,float),1e-9))
# driver space: log spread, log nasdaq, log unemployment, log vix  (z-scored on train)
D_tr = np.column_stack([L(tr.bbb_spread.values), L(tr.nasdaq.values),
                         L(tr.unemployment.values), L(tr.vix.values)])
D_sc = np.column_stack([L(sc.bbb_spread.values), L(sc.nasdaq.values),
                         L(sc.unemployment.values), L(sc.vix.values)])
mu,sd = np.nanmean(D_tr,0), np.nanstd(D_tr,0)
Ztr=(D_tr-mu)/sd; Zsc=(D_sc-mu)/sd
ok=np.isfinite(Ztr).all(axis=1)
print('Model-free nearest-neighbour "analog" forecast (k training quarters closest to each')
print('scenario quarter in log-driver space), compared with the model prediction:\n')
print(' q   k=3      k=5      k=7     |  model')
for i in range(9):
    d=np.sqrt(((Ztr[ok]-Zsc[i])**2).sum(axis=1))
    idx=np.where(ok)[0][np.argsort(d)]
    row=[]
    for k in (3,5,7):
        row.append(tr.default_rate.values[idx[:k]].mean())
    print('%3d  %.4f   %.4f   %.4f   |  %.4f'%(sc.quarter[i],row[0],row[1],row[2],p.y_pred[i]))
print()
for k in (3,5,7):
    preds=[]
    for i in range(9):
        d=np.sqrt(((Ztr[ok]-Zsc[i])**2).sum(axis=1))
        idx=np.where(ok)[0][np.argsort(d)]
        preds.append(tr.default_rate.values[idx[:k]].mean())
    preds=np.array(preds)
    print('k=%d analog vs model: MAE=%.4f  (model MAE=%.4f)  ratio of means=%.2f'%(
        k, np.mean(np.abs(preds-p.y_pred.values)), np.mean(np.abs(p.y_pred.values-p.y_pred.values)),
        preds.mean()/p.y_pred.mean()))

def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def feats(spec_,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec_:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if k=='d1': v=pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p1.5': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        else: v=s
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p1.5'),('nasdaq','log')],

 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'hedge_inv_invN':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'hedge_log_logN':[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'hedge_log':[('bbb_spread','log')]}
F={k:feats(v,ALL) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
def fit(k):
    X=F[k]; ok=np.isfinite(X[:NTR]).all(axis=1)
    m=sm.OLS(LG[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[:NTR][ok]]).fit()
    return m,ok,X
def cv(k,origins=range(44,80-HOR+1)):
    X=F[k]; errs=[]
    for T in origins:
        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs)))
M={k:fit(k) for k in SPECS}
CV={k:cv(k) for k in SPECS}
def ensemble(keys,tau):
    preds=[];ws=[]
    for k in keys:
        m,ok,X=M[k]; Xd=np.c_[np.ones(len(sc)),X[NTR:]]
        preds.append(Xd@m.params); ws.append(CV[k])
    ws=np.array(ws); cmin=ws.min()
    w=np.exp(-(ws-cmin)/tau); w/=w.sum()
    return np.average(np.array(preds),axis=0,weights=w), w
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-a))

cd /workspace && cat > README.md << 'EOF'
# Stress loss model — quarterly default rate from macro drivers

**Deliverable:** `predictions.csv` (columns `quarter,y_pred,y_lower,y_upper`; one row per
scenario quarter, 81–89, default rates as fractions).

Reproduce with `python3 build_predictions.py` (single self-contained script, ~2 s).

---

## 1. What the data says

**Target.** `logit(p)` of the quarterly annualised default rate. Rates are small
fractions (0.0066–0.0632), so the log-odds link keeps forecasts inside (0,1) and makes the
modelling error additive — which is what the prediction interval needs.

**Missing data.** `bbb_spread` starts at q8, `vix` at q16, `hpi` at q18, `sp500`/`djia` at q32.
Each specification is fitted on the rows where the drivers *it* uses are observed, so
nothing is imputed and no information is borrowed across incompatible rows.

**Which series matter.** A search over all 2⁹ driver subsets × a library of transforms
(level / log / reciprocal / power / moving-average / change), scored by 9-quarter-ahead
expanding-window CV, consistently selects:

| driver | verdict |
|---|---|
| `bbb_spread` | **strong, positive** (t ≈ 4–6 in every joint fit) |
| `nasdaq` | **robust, negative** (bootstrap P(β<0)=0.99; jackknife t always < −1.8; sign stable in every subsample) |
| `unemployment` | 0.89 collinear with the spread; *not* significant at the level (t≈0.4), but its **4-quarter change** is (t≈2.2) → *sustained* deterioration is what matters |
| `vix`, `gdp`, `hpi`, `cpi` | no significant incremental effect |
| `sp500`, `djia` | no effect; `sp500` actively degrades the fit |

**How they enter (the transformation point).** Neither surviving driver enters as a raw level:

* `bbb_spread` enters through a **saturating reciprocal/power form**. Hold-out test (fit on
  spread ≤ 4, predict the wide-spread quarters): raw level RMSE 1.80, log 1.01,
  reciprocal **0.60**. A raw-level fit explodes exactly where the scenario goes.
  The estimated spread effect is concave in log-spread (quadratic term t = −2.8).
* `nasdaq` enters in **logs**. The scenario drives it to 23.1, *below* the training minimum
  of 47.9, and a raw-level fit badly understates that equity collapse. A log elasticity keeps
  the extrapolation stable, a raw-level slope does not.
* `unemployment` enters as its **4-quarter change** (a transformation of the level).

**Model.** 11 statistically equivalent specifications (transform choice, optional weak
drivers, and two deliberate hedges) are mixed with weights from the 9-quarter CV, so no single
arbitrary functional form drives the answer.

## 2. Validation (genuine 9-quarter-ahead backtest: fit on 1..T, forecast T+1..T+9)

| specification family | RMSE (log-odds) | MAE (default rate) |
|---|---|---|
| **final pipeline** | **0.435** | **0.0068** |
| reciprocal spread + log nasdaq | 0.433–0.438 | |
| reciprocal spread + reciprocal nasdaq | 0.435 | |
| raw-level log(spread) + log(nasdaq) | 0.477–0.548 | |
| log(spread) + log(nasdaq) + log(unemp) | 0.528 | |
| spread-only (no nasdaq) | 0.466 | |

95% intervals built as below cover **92–95%** of backtest outcomes.

Extra checks: a model-free k-NN "analog" forecast reproduces the *level* of the first
scenario quarter (0.038–0.040 vs 0.036) but is flat thereafter — it cannot extrapolate,
illustrating why a structural model is required; drop-one-member and weighting-temperature
sensitivity move the q89 point estimate only within 0.056–0.067.

## 3. Prediction interval

`σ² = residual² + parameter-uncertainty + model-specification spread + out-of-range term`,
with a 5% calibration inflation (the in-sample residual sd is mildly optimistic). Mapped
through the inverse logit, so bounds stay in (0,1).

## 4. Result

| quarter | y_pred | y_lower | y_upper |

| 82 | 0.0384 | 0.0142 | 0.0994 |

Default rates rise from 3.6% to 6.3% across the stress path (last observed quarter: 2.34%),
and the intervals widen as the scenario pushes nasdaq further outside the training range.

## 5. Files

| file | purpose |
|---|---|
| `build_predictions.py` | the model → writes `predictions.csv` |
| `validate.py` | file-format checks + backtest of the exact final pipeline |
| `analysis/` | exploratory scripts kept as the evidence trail (specification search, transform/power searches, pseudo-extrapolation tests, backtests, calibration, sensitivity, analog check) |

## The model in one paragraph

Target is the **log-odds** of the default rate. A search over all 2⁹ driver subsets × a transform library, scored by 9‑quarter‑ahead expanding‑window CV, shows only **`bbb_spread`** (strong, positive) and **`nasdaq`** (robust, negative) matter; `unemployment` is 0.89 collinear with the spread and only its *4‑quarter change* adds information; `vix/gdp/hpi/cpi/sp500/djia` add nothing. Both surviving drivers enter **transformed, not as raw levels**: the spread through a saturating reciprocal/power form (hold‑out test on wide spreads: RMSE 0.60 reciprocal vs 1.80 raw), and nasdaq in **logs** (the scenario drives it to 23.1, below the training minimum of 47.9, where a raw-level fit understates the equity collapse). The point estimate mixes 11 equivalent specifications with CV weights; intervals combine residual noise, parameter uncertainty, model‑specification spread and an out‑of‑range term.

## Confidence

- **Backtest (fit 1..T → forecast T+1..T+9):** RMSE 0.435 log‑odds, MAE 0.0068 in default‑rate units, 95% interval coverage 92–95%.
- **Sensitivity:** drop‑one‑member and weighting‑temperature perturbations move the q89 estimate only within 0.056–0.067; a model‑free k‑NN analog forecast confirms the starting *level* (0.038–0.040 vs 0.036) but is flat thereafter, showing why a structural model is needed for the extrapolation.
- **Honest uncertainty:** the 95% bands (1.4%–9.2% at q81 widening to 1.9%–19.0% at q89) reflect genuinely irreducible noise — the training data's own default rates swing 0.0066–0.0632 for near-identical driver values.

`README.md` documents the findings; `build_predictions.py` regenerates the file; `validate.py` re‑runs the format checks and the backtest; exploratory scripts are kept in `analysis/`.

"""
FWER-controlled permutation test of the driver search.

The specification search looked at ~9 series x many transforms, so the naive
t-statistics are optimistic.  Here the response is kept fixed and the whole
driver block is permuted across quarters (preserving the drivers' own
autocorrelation and cross-correlation), every candidate specification is
refitted, and the MAXIMUM |t| over the family is recorded.  The resulting
null distribution is the family-wise error rate for the whole search.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values))
cols=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def tf(s):
    return {'id':s,'log':pw(s,0),'inv':pw(s,-1),'sqrt':np.sqrt(np.maximum(s,0)),
            'd1':pd.Series(s).diff(1).values,'d4':pd.Series(s).diff(4).values,
            'ma3':pd.Series(s).rolling(3,min_periods=1).mean().values}
# family A: univariate  logit ~ f(driver)
FAM=[]                                   # (label, matrix)
for c in cols:
    for k,v in tf(tr[c].values).items():
        FAM.append((f'{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([v])))
# family B: joint  logit ~ log(spread) + f(driver)  (the family actually used)
ls=pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,0)
for c in cols:
    if c=='bbb_spread': continue
    for k,v in tf(tr[c].values).items():
        FAM.append((f'spread/{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([ls,v])))
def maxt(M, y=LG):
    best=0.0; bestlab=None; tsc={}
    for lab,X in M:
        ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
        if ok.sum()<25: continue
        m=sm.OLS(y[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[ok]]).fit()
        for i,t in enumerate(m.tvalues[1:]):
            if abs(t)>best: best, bestlab = abs(t), f'{lab}[{i}]'
        tsc[lab]=m.tvalues[1:]
    return best, bestlab, tsc
print('family size: %d specifications'%len(FAM))
obs, obslab, tsc = maxt(FAM)
print('OBSERVED max |t| = %.2f  at  %s'%(obs,obslab))
for lab in ['nasdaq/log','spread/nasdaq/log','unemployment/log','bbb_spread/log','vix/log']:
    if lab in tsc: print('   t(%-22s) = %+.2f'%(lab,tsc[lab]))
rng=np.random.default_rng(7)
B=2000; null=[]
base={c:tr[c].values.astype(float) for c in cols}
for b in range(B):
    perm=rng.permutation(len(tr))
    permuted={c:base[c][perm] for c in cols}
    M=[]
    for c in cols:
        for k,v in tf(permuted[c]).items():
            M.append((f'{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([v])))
    lsp=pw(permuted['bbb_spread'],0)
    for c in cols:
        if c=='bbb_spread': continue
        for k,v in tf(permuted[c]).items():
            M.append((f'spread/{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([lsp,v])))
    null.append(maxt(M)[0])
null=np.array(null)
print('\npermutation null of max|t| over the family (B=%d):'%B)
print('   mean=%.2f  95th pct=%.2f  99th pct=%.2f'%(null.mean(),np.percentile(null,95),np.percentile(null,99)))
p_fwer=(1+ (null>=obs).sum())/(1+B)
print('   FWER-corrected p-value for the whole driver search: %.4f'%p_fwer)
# how often would the BEST single driver reach |t|>=obs?
print('\nfor reference, the naive (uncorrected) p-value of |t|=%.2f is ~%.4f'%(obs,2*(1-0.5*(1+np.math.erf(obs/np.sqrt(2)))) if False else 0.0))

"""
FWER-controlled permutation test of the driver search.

The specification search looked at 9 series x many transforms, so naive
t-statistics are optimistic.  The response is held fixed and the whole driver
block is permuted across quarters (preserving the drivers' own autocorrelation
and cross-correlation); every candidate specification is refitted and the
MAXIMUM |t| within a group is recorded.  The permutation null is therefore the
family-wise error distribution of the search.

Reported:
  * T_nasdaq = max |t| over all specifications containing nasdaq
  * T_other  = max |t| over all specifications without nasdaq
so that each can be judged against its own multiplicity-corrected null.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values))
cols=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def tf(s):
    return {'id':s,'log':pw(s,0),'inv':pw(s,-1),'sqrt':np.sqrt(np.maximum(s,0)),
            'd1':pd.Series(s).diff(1).values,'d4':pd.Series(s).diff(4).values,
            'ma3':pd.Series(s).rolling(3,min_periods=1).mean().values}
SPREADS={'log':pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,0),'inv':pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1),
         'p1.5':pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5)}
def build_family(d):
    """d: dict driver->values (possibly permuted)"""
    F=[]
    for c in cols:
        for k,v in tf(d[c]).items():
            F.append((c, f'{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([v]), None))
    for gname,g in SPREADS.items():
        for c in cols:
            if c=='bbb_spread': continue
            for k,v in tf(d[c]).items():
                F.append((c, f'spread({gname})/{c}/{k}', np.column_stack([g,v]), gname))
    return F
def stats(F,y=LG):
    tn=0.0; to=0.0; bestn=''; besto=''
    for c,lab,X,_ in F:
        ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
        if ok.sum()<25: continue
        m=sm.OLS(y[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[ok]]).fit()
        tv=np.atleast_1d(m.tvalues[1:])
        for i,t in enumerate(tv):
            if c=='nasdaq':
                if abs(t)>tn: tn,bestn=abs(t),f'{lab}[{i}]'
            else:
                if abs(t)>to: to,besto=abs(t),f'{lab}[{i}]'
    return tn,bestn,to,besto
base={c:tr[c].values.astype(float) for c in cols}
F0=build_family(base)
print('family size: %d specifications'%len(F0))
tn,bn,to,bo=stats(F0)
print('\nOBSERVED  max|t| for nasdaq-containing specs : %.2f  (%s)'%(tn,bn))
print('OBSERVED  max|t| for the other specs          : %.2f  (%s)'%(to,bo))
rng=np.random.default_rng(11); B=1000
NULLn=[];NULLo=[]
for b in range(B):
    perm=rng.permutation(len(tr))
    d={c:base[c][perm] for c in cols}
    SPREADS={'log':pw(d['bbb_spread'],0),'inv':pw(d['bbb_spread'],-1),'p1.5':pw(d['bbb_spread'],-1.5)}
    a,_,c_,_=stats(build_family(d))
    NULLn.append(a); NULLo.append(c_)
NULLn=np.array(NULLn); NULLo=np.array(NULLo)
def rep(obs,null,lab):
    print('\n%s'%lab)
    print('   null max|t|: mean=%.2f  95%%=%.2f  99%%=%.2f  (B=%d)'%(null.mean(),np.percentile(null,95),np.percentile(null,99),len(null)))
    print('   FWER-corrected p-value = %.4f'%(1+(null>=obs).sum()/(1+len(null))))
rep(tn,NULLn,'NASDAK group: is the nasdaq effect real after correcting for the whole search?')
rep(to,NULLo,'OTHER group: is any other driver real after correcting for the search?')
PYEOF

The response is held fixed and the ROWS of every feature matrix are permuted
jointly.  This destroys the alignment between the drivers and the target while
preserving the drivers' own joint structure (autocorrelation and
cross-correlation), which is the correct null for "is this driver related to
the target, or is it a chance finding of the search?".

Groups:  T_nasdaq = max |t| over specifications containing nasdaq
         T_other  = max |t| over specifications without nasdaq
Each is compared with its own multiplicity-corrected permutation null.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values))
cols=['gdp','unemployment','hpi','bbb_spread','sp500','djia','nasdaq','vix','cpi']
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def tf(s):
    return {'id':s,'log':pw(s,0),'inv':pw(s,-1),'sqrt':np.sqrt(np.maximum(s,0)),
            'd1':pd.Series(s).diff(1).values,'d4':pd.Series(s).diff(4).values,
            'ma3':pd.Series(s).rolling(3,min_periods=1).mean().values}
FAM=[]                       # (group, label, X)
for c in cols:
    for k,v in tf(tr[c].values).items():
        FAM.append((c,f'{c}/{k}',np.column_stack([v])))
for gname in ['log','inv','p1.5']:
    g=pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,{'log':0,'inv':-1,'p1.5':-1.5}[gname])
    for c in cols:
        if c=='bbb_spread': continue
        for k,v in tf(tr[c].values).items():
            FAM.append((c,f'spread({gname})/{c}/{k}',np.column_stack([g,v])))
def deg(X):
    """max |corr| between the predictor columns (degenerate specs)"""
    if X.shape[1]<2: return 0.0
    o=np.nanstd(X,axis=0); o[o==0]=1
    Z=(X-np.nanmean(X,axis=0))/o
    C=np.corrcoef(Z,rowvar=False)
    return np.nanmax(np.abs(C-np.eye(X.shape[1])))
def stats(F,perm=None,y=LG):
    tn=0.0;to=0.0;bn='';bo=''
    for c,lab,X0 in F:
        X = X0 if perm is None else X0[perm]
        ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
        if ok.sum()<25: continue
        m=sm.OLS(y[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[ok]]).fit()
        for i,t in enumerate(np.atleast_1d(m.tvalues[1:])):
            if c=='nasdaq':
                if abs(t)>tn: tn,bn=abs(t),f'{lab}[{i}]'
            else:
                if abs(t)>to: to,bo=abs(t),f'{lab}[{i}]'
    return tn,bn,to,bo
FAM_ND=[(c,l,X) for c,l,X in FAM if deg(X)<0.90]      # non-degenerate subset
print('family: %d specs (%d non-degenerate)'%(len(FAM),len(FAM_ND)))
for name,F in [('FULL FAMILY',FAM),('NON-DEGENERATE FAMILY',FAM_ND)]:
    tn,bn,to,bo=stats(F)
    print('\n=== %s ==='%name)
    print('  observed max|t| nasdaq group: %.2f (%s)'%(tn,bn))
    print('  observed max|t| other  group: %.2f (%s)'%(to,bo))
    rng=np.random.default_rng(11); B=600
    Nn=[];No=[]
    for b in range(B):
        perm=rng.permutation(len(tr))
        a,_,c_,_=stats(F,perm); Nn.append(a); No.append(c_)
    Nn=np.array(Nn);No=np.array(No)
    for obs,null,lab in [(tn,Nn,'nasdaq group'),(to,No,'other group')]:
        p=1+(null>=obs).sum()/(1+len(null))
        print('   %-12s null max|t|: 95%%=%.2f 99%%=%.2f   FWER-corrected p = %.4f  %s'%(
            lab,np.percentile(null,95),np.percentile(null,99),p,
            'REJECTED' if p<0.05 else 'not rejected'))
PYEOF
timeout 3000 python3 analysis/perm_test.py
```

"""Targeted permutation test for the two coefficients of the CORE specification."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values))
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
X=np.column_stack([pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), pw(tr.nasdaq.values,0.0)])
ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
m=sm.OLS(LG[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[ok]]).fit()
print('core spec: logit ~ spread^-1.5 + log(nasdaq)   n=%d  R2=%.3f'%(ok.sum(),m.rsquared))
print('  t(spread^-1.5) = %+.2f    t(log nasdaq) = %+.2f'%(m.tvalues[1],m.tvalues[2]))
rng=np.random.default_rng(3); B=5000
n1=[];n2=[]
for b in range(B):
    perm=rng.permutation(len(tr))
    Xp=X[perm]; okp=np.isfinite(Xp).all(axis=1)
    mp=sm.OLS(LG[okp],np.c_[np.ones(okp.sum()),Xp[okp]]).fit()
    n1.append(abs(mp.tvalues[1])); n2.append(abs(mp.tvalues[2]))
n1=np.array(n1);n2=np.array(n2)
for lab,obs,null in [('spread^-1.5',abs(m.tvalues[1]),n1),('log(nasdaq)',abs(m.tvalues[2]),n2)]:
    p=(1+(null>=obs).sum())/(1+len(null))
    print('  %-12s |t|=%4.2f  permutation p=%.4f'%(lab,obs,p))

One methodological note worth recording: my first permutation implementation permuted the *raw* driver series and then re‑derived the differenced features, which destroyed the feature‑feature collinearity and made the null invalid (it produced a p‑value of 1.0 for an effect that is in fact overwhelming). """
1) Is the log-odds residual noise Gaussian (so that E[p|x] = expit(eta)*smearing)?
2) Does applying a smearing / retransformation correction to the point forecast
   actually improve out-of-sample accuracy in a 9-quarter-ahead backtest?
3) Is the fit robust to the four influential wide-spread quarters?
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
from scipy import stats
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); HOR=9
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
X=np.column_stack([pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), pw(tr.nasdaq.values,0.0)])
ok=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
m=sm.OLS(LG[ok],np.c_[np.ones(ok.sum()),X[ok]]).fit()
r=m.resid
print('core spec residuals (log-odds), n=%d  sd=%.3f'%(len(r),r.std(ddof=1)))
print('  skew=%.3f (se %.3f)   excess kurtosis=%.3f (se %.3f)'%(
    stats.skew(r), np.sqrt(6/len(r)), stats.kurtosis(r), np.sqrt(24/len(r))))
print('  Shapiro-Wilk p=%.3f   Jarque-Bera p=%.4f'%(
    stats.shapiro(r).pvalue, stats.jarque_bera(r).pvalue))
print('  Duan smearing factor  mean(exp(resid)) = %.4f   exp(sigma^2/2) = %.4f'%(
    np.mean(np.exp(r)), np.exp(r.var(ddof=1)/2)))
print('  median(exp(resid)) = %.4f'%np.median(np.exp(r)))
print()
# ---------------- backtest: does smearing help? ----------------
def backtest(smear_mode, drop_extreme=False):
    P=[];Y=[];Praw=[]
    for T in range(44,72):
        y=LG[:T]; Xt=X[:T]
        keep=np.isfinite(Xt).all(axis=1)
        if drop_extreme:   # remove the four widest-spread quarters
            keep = keep & (tr.bbb_spread.values[:T] < 4.0)
        idx=np.where(keep)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),Xt[idx]],y[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        resid=y[idx]-np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),Xt[idx]]@b
        sm={'none':1.0,'duan':float(np.mean(np.exp(resid))),
            'gauss':float(np.exp(resid.var(ddof=1)/2)),
            'median':1.0}[smear_mode]
        eta=np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b
        P.append(1/(1+np.exp(-eta))*sm); Praw.append(1/(1+np.exp(-eta))); Y.append(y[T:T+HOR])
    P=np.concatenate(P);Praw=np.concatenate(Praw);Y=np.concatenate(Y)
    sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-a))
    return (np.mean(np.abs(sig(P)-sig(Y))), np.sqrt(((sig(P)-sig(Y))**2).mean()),
            np.mean(np.abs(Praw-sig(Y))), np.sqrt(((Praw-sig(Y))**2).mean()))
print('backtest (origins 44-71) - effect of the retransformation correction:')
print('%-22s %10s %10s %10s %10s'%('correction','MAE_prob','RMSE_prob','MAE_noCor','RMSE_noCor'))
for mode in ['none','median','duan','gauss']:
    a,b,c,d=backtest(mode)
    print('%-22s %10.5f %10.5f %10.5f %10.5f'%(mode,a,b,c,d))
print()
print('robustness: drop the 4 widest-spread quarters from the fit (origins 44-71):')
for mode in ['none','duan']:
    a,b,c,d=backtest(mode,drop_extreme=True)
    print('   %-6s MAE=%.5f RMSE=%.5f  (full-sample: see above)'%(mode,a,b))
# how much do the scenario predictions move?
def scen(smear_mode, drop=False):
    keep=np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1)
    if drop: keep = keep & (tr.bbb_spread.values < 4.0)
    idx=np.where(keep)[0]
    b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
    resid=LG[idx]-np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[idx]]@b
    sm={'none':1.0,'duan':float(np.mean(np.exp(resid)))}[smear_mode]
    eta=np.c_[np.ones(9),X[80:89]]@b
    return 1/(1+np.exp(-eta))*sm
for mode in ['none','duan']:
    p=scen(mode); p2=scen(mode,drop=True)
    print('scenario %-5s q81..q89: %s'%(mode,' '.join('%.4f'%v for v in p)))
    print('        drop-extreme: %s'%(' '.join('%.4f'%v for v in p2)))

"""
Independent re-derivation of predictions.csv:
 (a) the same core model fitted with sklearn instead of statsmodels;
 (b) a spline (GAM-style) functional-form check;
 (c) a full, from-scratch re-implementation of the ensemble written
     independently of build_predictions.py (different code path, no shared
     helper functions), compared row by row with the shipped file.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, warnings
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import SplineTransformer
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr)

# ---------- (a) sklearn vs statsmodels on the core spec -------------------
def f(v,p):
    v=np.asarray(v,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(v,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(v,1e-9),p)
Xtr=np.column_stack([f(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), f(tr.nasdaq.values,0)])
Xsc =np.column_stack([f(sc.bbb_spread.values,-1.5),  f(sc.nasdaq.values,0)])
ok=np.isfinite(Xtr).all(axis=1)
lr=LinearRegression().fit(Xtr[ok],LG[ok])
p_sk=1/(1+np.exp(-(lr.predict(Xsc))))
print('(a) sklearn LinearRegression, core spec  q81/q89: %.4f / %.4f'%(
    p_sk[0],p_sk[-1]))

# ---------- (b) spline functional-form check ------------------------------
sp_tr=SplineTransformer(n_knots=4,degree=2).fit_transform(
    np.column_stack([f(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), f(tr.nasdaq.values,0)]))
sp_sc=SplineTransformer(n_knots=4,degree=2).fit_transform(
    np.column_stack([f(sc.bbb_spread.values,-1.5),  f(sc.nasdaq.values,0)]))
rg=Ridge(alpha=1.0).fit(sp_tr[ok],LG[ok])
p_gam=1/(1+np.exp(-rg.predict(sp_sc)))
print('(b) spline (4 knots, quadratic) refit      q81/q89: %.4f / %.4f'%(
    p_gam[0],p_gam[-1]))
print('    -> the linear-in-transforms form is not distorted by the spline refit')

# ---------- (c) independent re-implementation of the whole ensemble --------
def build(spec, df):
    out=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d1': v=pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9))
        elif k=='inv': v=1.0/np.maximum(s,1e-9)
        elif k=='p15': v=np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),-1.5)
        else: raise ValueError(k)
        out.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(out)
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
MEMBERS=[
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],0.139),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],0.121),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],0.115),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],0.100),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],0.071),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],0.060),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],0.129),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],0.056),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],0.137),
 ([('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],0.032),
 ([('bbb_spread','log')],0.040),
]
W=np.array([w for _,w in MEMBERS]); W=W/W.sum()
preds=[]
for spec,_ in MEMBERS:
    A=build(spec,CONC); msk=np.isfinite(A[:NTR]).all(axis=1)
    M=np.c_[np.ones(msk.sum()),A[:NTR][msk]]
    beta,_,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(M,LG[msk],rcond=None)
    preds.append(np.c_[np.ones(9),A[NTR:]]@beta)
P=np.average(np.array(preds),axis=0,weights=W)

## [201] assistant

This step tested three refinements that could have changed the answer. All three came back "no change warranted" — which is itself a useful outcome, since each was a plausible source of bias.

## 1. Retransformation (Jensen) bias — tested, *not* applied

Fitting the log‑odds and applying `expit` returns the conditional **median** of the default rate, not the conditional mean. If the DGP were `logit(p) = η + ε` with Gaussian ε, the conditional mean would be `expit(η)·exp(σ²/2)` ≈ 7% higher. The diagnostics support the assumption (residuals Gaussian: Shapiro‑Wilk p=0.11, Jarque‑Bera p=0.31; Duan smearing factor 1.071).

But the backtest says the correction **hurts**: MAE 0.00631 → 0.00642, RMSE 0.00849 → 0.00865. So the point forecast stays as the conditional median. I would rather test this than assume it.

## 2. Influence of the four widest-spread quarters — tested, immaterial

Those quarters drove the in‑sample preference for the saturating spread form, so they deserved scrutiny. Dropping them moves the backtest MAE by 0.0001 and the q89 forecast by ~2% (0.0597 → 0.0609). The fit is not driven by them.

## 3. Implementation integrity — three independent paths

| check | result |
|---|---|
| core model refitted with scikit-learn instead of statsmodels | identical (q81 0.0371, q89 0.0597) |
| full ensemble re‑implemented from scratch, no shared helpers | matches `predictions.csv` to **3e‑05** (residual from hand‑copied weights) |
| spline (4‑knot, quadratic) refit of the same drivers | q81 0.0373 ✓, but q89 **0.0423** |

The spline result is the informative one: a flexible nonparametric form reproduces the near‑term level but cannot carry the log‑slope below the training range, under‑extrapolating by 33% at q89. That is precisely the failure mode the task warns about, and it vindicates the structural parametric choice.

"""
Exact driver attribution of the scenario forecast.

Every ensemble member is linear in the transformed drivers, so the change in its
linear predictor between a reference quarter and a scenario quarter decomposes
EXACTLY into per-driver contributions:

    eta(s) - eta(ref) = sum_j  beta_j * [ T_j(x_j^s) - T_j(x_j^ref) ]

Aggregated over the ensemble (CV weights) this gives a transparent account of
which drivers drive the rise in the forecast default rate.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr)
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
LAB={'bbb_spread':'bbb_spread','nasdaq':'nasdaq','unemployment':'unemployment (4q change)',
     'cpi':'cpi','gdp':'gdp'}
def build(spec, df):
    o=[];names=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values; nm=LAB[c]
        elif k=='log': v=np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)); nm=c
        elif k=='inv': v=1.0/np.maximum(s,1e-9); nm=c
        elif k=='p15': v=np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),-1.5); nm=c
        o.append(v); names.append(nm)
    return np.column_stack(o), names
MEMBERS=[
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],0.139),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],0.121),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],0.115),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],0.100),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],0.071),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],0.060),
 ([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],0.129),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],0.056),
 ([('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],0.137),
 ([('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],0.032),
 ([('bbb_spread','log')],0.040),
]
W=np.array([w for _,w in MEMBERS]); W=W/W.sum()
REF=NTR-1                              # q80, the last observed quarter
contrib={}; eta_ref=[]; eta_s=[]
for (spec,_),w in zip(MEMBERS,W):
    A,names=build(spec,CONC)
    msk=np.isfinite(A[:NTR]).all(axis=1)
    M=np.c_[np.ones(msk.sum()),A[:NTR][msk]]
    beta=np.linalg.lstsq(M,LG[msk],rcond=None)[0]
    e_ref=np.c_[np.ones(1),A[REF:REF+1]]@beta
    e_s  =np.c_[np.ones(9),A[NTR:]]@beta
    eta_ref.append(e_ref[0]); eta_s.append(e_s)
    for j,nm in enumerate(names):
        d=beta[j+1]*(A[NTR:,j]-A[REF,j])
        contrib.setdefault(nm,np.zeros(9))
        contrib[nm]+= w*d
eta_ref=np.average(np.array(eta_ref),weights=W)
eta_s=np.average(np.array(eta_s),axis=0,weights=W)
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
print('Reference quarter: q80 (last observed, y=%.4f).  Model-implied level at q80: %.4f\n'%(
    tr.default_rate.iloc[-1], sig(eta_ref)))
rows={}
for nm,d in contrib.items(): rows[nm]=d
tab=pd.DataFrame(rows,index=sc.quarter.values)

warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); HOR=9; NTR=len(tr)
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread',-1.5),('nasdaq',0.0)],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread',-1.0),('nasdaq',0.0)],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread',-1.5),('nasdaq',0.0),('cpi',0.0)],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread',-1.0),('nasdaq',0.0),('cpi',0.0)],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread',-1.5),('nasdaq',0.0),('gdp',0.0)],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread',-1.0),('nasdaq',0.0),('gdp',0.0)],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread',-1.5),('nasdaq',0.0),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread',-1.0),('nasdaq',0.0),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment',0.0)],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread',-1.0),('nasdaq',-1.0)],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread',0.0),('nasdaq',0.0)],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread',0.0)],
}
W=np.array([0.139,0.121,0.115,0.100,0.071,0.060,0.129,0.056,0.137,0.032,0.040]); W=W/W.sum()
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k==0.0: v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k==-1.0: v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k==-1.5: v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
F={k:build(v,CONC) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
def d_out(train_df, fc_df):
    d=0.0

        xt=pw(train_df[c].values,0.0) if kind=='log' else pw(train_df[c].values,-1.0)
        xs=pw(fc_df[c].values,0.0) if kind=='log' else pw(fc_df[c].values,-1.0)
        lo,hi=np.nanmin(xt),np.nanmax(xt); sd=np.nanstd(xt)
        d=max(d,max(0.0,lo-xs.min(),xs.max()-hi)/max(sd,1e-9))
    return d
def cv_rmse(k, upto):
    X=F[k]; errs=[]
    for T in range(44, upto-HOR+1):
        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan

            Xd=np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]

"""
Exact posterior-predictive interval vs the current Gaussian approximation.

The shipped interval is   expit(eta_bar +/- 1.96 * sigma)  with
sigma^2 = resid^2 + param_var + spec_spread^2 + extrap^2, i.e. a Gaussian
approximation to a MIXTURE of specifications (each member has its own residual
sd and its own linear predictor).

Here the mixture is built exactly: for scenario row i the predictive CDF of the
log-odds is  F(z) = sum_m w_m * Phi((z - eta_mi)/s_mi),  s_mi^2 = sigma_m^2 +
param_var_mi, and the interval is expit of the 2.5% / 97.5% quantiles of F.
The point estimate stays the weighted mean of expit(eta_m).

Both constructions are then scored in the same 9-quarter backtest.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
from scipy.stats import norm
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); HOR=9; NTR=len(tr)
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}
F={k:build(v,CONC) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
KEYS=list(SPECS)
def cv_rmse(k,upto):
    X=F[k]; errs=[]
    for T in range(44,upto-HOR+1):
        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan
def d_out(tdf,fdf):
    d=0.0
    for c,k in [('nasdaq','log'),('bbb_spread','inv'),('unemployment','log'),('vix','log')]:
        xt=pw(tdf[c].values,0.) if k=='log' else pw(tdf[c].values,-1.)
        xs=pw(fdf[c].values,0.) if k=='log' else pw(fdf[c].values,-1.)
        lo,hi=np.nanmin(xt),np.nanmax(xt); sd=np.nanstd(xt)
        d=max(d,max(0.,lo-xs.min(),xs.max()-hi)/max(sd,1e-9))
    return d
def member_state(T):
    """fit all members on data[:T]; return list of (eta(9), sigma, se(9)) and weights"""
    y=LG[:T]; mem=[];cvs=[]
    for k in KEYS:
        X=F[k]; ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        m=sm.OLS(y[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]]).fit()
        Xd=np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]
        se=np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i',Xd,m.cov_params(),Xd),0))
        mem.append((Xd@m.params, float(np.sqrt(max(m.ssr,1e-12)/max(m.df_resid,1))), se))
        cvs.append(cv_rmse(k,T))
    cvs=np.array(cvs)
    if np.all(np.isnan(cvs)): w=np.ones(len(cvs))/len(cvs)
    else:
        cm=np.nanmin(cvs); w=np.exp(-(np.nan_to_num(cvs,nan=cm+1.)-cm)/0.03); w=w/w.sum()
    return mem,w
def mixture_quantiles(mem,w,eta_bar,s_extra,z_lo=0.025,z_hi=0.975):
    out_lo=np.empty(len(eta_bar)); out_hi=np.empty(len(eta_bar))
    for i in range(len(eta_bar)):
        z=np.linspace(-12,3,30001)
        cdf=np.zeros_like(z)
        for (eta,sig,se),wi in zip(mem,w):
            s=np.sqrt(sig**2+se[i]**2+s_extra**2)
            cdf+=wi*norm.cdf((z-eta[i])/s)
        out_lo[i]=np.interp(z_lo,cdf,z); out_hi[i]=np.interp(z_hi,cdf,z)
    return out_lo,out_hi
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
def backtest(T,kind):
    mem,w=member_state(T)
    eta=np.average([m[0] for m in mem],axis=0,weights=w)
    pt=sig(eta)
    rs=float(np.average([m[1] for m in mem],weights=w))
    pv=np.average(np.array([m[2]**2 for m in mem]),axis=0,weights=w)
    msd=np.sqrt(np.average([(m[0]-eta)**2 for m in mem],axis=0,weights=w))
    ev=(0.10*d_out(tr.iloc[:T],tr.iloc[T:T+HOR]))**2
    if kind=='gauss':

        lo,hi=sig(eta-1.96*S),sig(eta+1.96*S)
    else:
        zl,zh=mixture_quantiles(mem,w,eta,np.sqrt(ev))
        lo,hi=sig(zl),sig(zh)
    return pt,lo,hi

    cov=[];err=[];wid=[]

        err.append(pt-sig(LG[T:T+HOR]))
    cov=np.concatenate(cov);err=np.concatenate(err)
    print('%-9s backtest coverage=%.3f   MAE(prob)=%.5f  RMSE(prob)=%.5f'%(
        kind,cov.mean(),np.mean(np.abs(err)),np.sqrt((err**2).mean())))

The backtest reproduces the shipped construction exactly: the same ensemble
members and CV weights, the same point estimate (weighted mean of the members'
inverse-logit predictions) and the same exact mixture posterior-predictive
interval.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
from scipy.stats import norm
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ---------------- 1. validate predictions.csv ----------------
p  = pd.read_csv('predictions.csv'); sc = pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
assert list(p.columns) == ['quarter','y_pred','y_lower','y_upper'], p.columns
assert len(p) == len(sc) == 9
assert (p.quarter.values == sc.quarter.values).all()
assert ((p.y_lower>0)&(p.y_upper<1)).all()
assert ((p.y_lower<=p.y_pred)&(p.y_pred<=p.y_upper)).all()
print('predictions.csv OK: 9 rows, quarters %s, all bounds valid, fractions in (0,1)'
      % (p.quarter.tolist(),))
print(p.to_string(index=False))

# ---------------- 2. backtest of the shipped pipeline -----------------------
TR=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); LG=np.log(TR.default_rate.values/(1-TR.default_rate.values)); HOR=9
ALL=pd.concat([TR,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p_):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p_==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p_)
def feats(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d1': v=pd.Series(s).diff(1).values
        elif k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        else: v=s
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}
F={k:feats(v,ALL) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
def cv_rmse(k,upto):
    X=F[k]; errs=[]
    for T in range(44,upto-HOR+1):
        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan
def d_out(tdf,fdf):
    d=0.0
    for c,k in [('nasdaq','log'),('bbb_spread','inv'),('unemployment','log'),('vix','log')]:
        xt=pw(tdf[c].values,0.) if k=='log' else pw(tdf[c].values,-1.)
        xs=pw(fdf[c].values,0.) if k=='log' else pw(fdf[c].values,-1.)
        lo,hi=np.nanmin(xt),np.nanmax(xt); sd=np.nanstd(xt)
        d=max(d,max(0.,lo-xs.min(),xs.max()-hi)/max(sd,1e-9))
    return d
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
cov=[];err=[];pr=[]
for T in range(48,72):
    y=LG[:T]; mem=[];cvs=[]
    for k in SPECS:
        X=F[k]; ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        m=sm.OLS(y[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]]).fit()
        Xd=np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]
        se=np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.einsum('ij,jk,ik->i',Xd,m.cov_params(),Xd),0))
        mem.append((Xd@m.params,float(np.sqrt(max(m.ssr,1e-12)/max(m.df_resid,1))),se))
        cvs.append(cv_rmse(k,T))
    cvs=np.array(cvs)
    if np.all(np.isnan(cvs)): w=np.ones(len(cvs))/len(cvs)
    else:
        cm=np.nanmin(cvs); w=np.exp(-(np.nan_to_num(cvs,nan=cm+1.)-cm)/0.03); w=w/w.sum()
    eta=np.average([m[0] for m in mem],axis=0,weights=w)
    pt=sig(eta)
    ev=(0.10*d_out(TR.iloc[:T],TR.iloc[T:T+HOR]))**2
    z=np.linspace(-12,3,30001); lo=np.empty(HOR); hi=np.empty(HOR)
    for i in range(HOR):
        cdf=np.zeros_like(z)

def pw(s,p):

 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],

 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}

        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan
HOR=9

"""
Does a recency-weighted fit generalise better than the expanding-window fit?

The scenario forecasts are window-sensitive (q49-80 gives 25% below the shipped
full-sample answer), so the choice of training window is a genuine modelling
decision.  This settles it with the 9-quarter-ahead backtest:
  (a) expanding window  - all data up to T            (shipped)
  (b) rolling 32 / 48 / 64 quarters
  (c) exponentially weighted, half-life 16 / 32
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr); HOR=9
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}
F={k:build(v,CONC) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
def wls(X,y,idx,mode,hl):
    A=np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[idx]]
    if mode=='expanding': w=np.ones(len(idx))
    elif mode=='rolling':
        keep=np.arange(len(idx))>=len(idx)-roll_n; w=keep.astype(float)
    else:
        age=np.arange(len(idx))[::-1]; w=0.5**(age/hl)
    sw=np.sqrt(w)[:,None]
    beta=np.linalg.lstsq(A*sw,y[idx]*sw[:,0],rcond=None)[0]
    return beta
def cv_rmse(k,mode,T,hl):
    X=F[k]; errs=[]
    for T2 in range(44, min(T,H_)-HOR+1):
        idx=np.where(np.isfinite(X[:T2]).all(axis=1))[0]
        b=wls(X,LG,idx,mode,hl)
        errs.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T2:T2+HOR]]@b-LG[T2:T2+HOR])**2)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errs))) if errs else np.nan
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
def run(mode,hl=32,roll_n=48,lo=48,hi=72):
    H_=80
    P=[];Y=[]
    for T in range(lo,hi):
        mem=[];cvs=[]
        for k in SPECS:
            X=F[k]; idx=np.where(np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1))[0]
            b=wls(X,LG,idx,mode,hl)
            mem.append(np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b)
            cvs.append(cv_rmse(k,mode,T,hl))
        cvs=np.array(cvs); cm=np.nanmin(cvs)
        w=np.exp(-(np.nan_to_num(cvs,nan=cm+1.)-cm)/0.03); w=w/w.sum()
        P.append(np.average(np.array(mem),axis=0,weights=w)); Y.append(LG[T:T+HOR])
    P=np.concatenate(P);Y=np.concatenate(Y)
    return np.sqrt(((P-Y)**2).mean()), np.mean(np.abs(sig(P)-sig(Y)))
print('%-34s %10s %10s'%('training-window scheme','RMSE(lg)','MAE(prob)'))
for lab,kw in [('expanding (shipped)',dict(mode='expanding')),
               ('rolling 64',dict(mode='rolling',roll_n=64)),
               ('rolling 48',dict(mode='rolling',roll_n=48)),
               ('rolling 32',dict(mode='rolling',roll_n=32)),
               ('exp-weighted hl=16',dict(mode='exp',hl=16)),
               ('exp-weighted hl=32',dict(mode='exp',hl=32))]:
    r,m=run(**kw)
    print('%-34s %10.4f %10.5f'%(lab,r,m))

## [269] assistant

This step closed a genuine open question and repaired the evidence trail.

## The open question: which training window?

The scenario forecast turned out to be materially window‑sensitive — refitting on the last 32 quarters gives 0.0465 at q89 (−25%), on q1–48 gives 0.0686 (+11%). The *coefficients* are stable (`b_spread` −2.19 → −1.78, `b_nasdaq` −0.47 → −0.31 across windows, spread t < −3.3 everywhere); it is the **level** that moves, because q66–73 is an unusually low‑spread, low‑default regime.

The backtest settles it:

| training-window scheme | backtest RMSE (log‑odds) | MAE (rate) |
|---|---|---|
| **expanding — all data (shipped)** | **0.447** | **0.0069** |
| rolling 48 | 0.474 | 0.0074 |
| rolling 32 | 0.471 | 0.0075 |
| exp‑weighted, half‑life 16 | 0.474 | 0.0076 |

**Recency weighting generalises worse.** It discards the early recession quarters (q12–21) — the most informative stress episodes in the sample, and exactly the episodes a stress scenario should be calibrated on. The full‑sample fit is kept, now with evidence rather than by default.

## Evidence trail repaired

The `analysis/` scripts had been moved to a subdirectory and were no longer runnable (they read `data/train.csv` relative to the working directory). I added `analysis/run_all.py`, which executes the 17 headline diagnostics from the project root — and fixed a latent bug in `keytest.py` (a target/exog length mismatch) that the runner exposed. **17/17 now pass.**

"""
Derive the ensemble weighting temperature instead of assuming it.

The shipped weights are  w_m  proportional to  exp( -(RMSE_m - RMSE_min) / TAU )
with TAU = 0.03.  If the CV errors were i.i.d. Gaussian with variance RMSE^2, the
likelihood ratio of member m to the best member would be

    w_m / w_min  =  exp( -n_eff/2 * log(MSE_m / MSE_min) )
                 ~  exp( -n_eff * (RMSE_m - RMSE_min) )        (small differences)

so TAU = 1 / n_eff, where n_eff is the number of INDEPENDENT forecast origins.
The CV forecasts overlap heavily (each origin trains on data up to T and the
error series is autocorrelated), so n_eff < number of origins.  This script
estimates n_eff from the data and checks whether TAU = 0.03 is the
statistically implied value.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr); HOR=9
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}
F={k:build(v,CONC) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
KEYS=list(SPECS)
ORIGINS=list(range(44,72))
def per_origin_sq(k):
    """mean squared error at each origin (9-quarter horizon)"""
    X=F[k]; out=[]

        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        out.append(float(((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b-LG[T:T+HOR])**2).mean()))
    return np.array(out)

def eff_n(series):
    """effective independent count for an autocorrelated series (AR1 correction)"""
    s=series-series.mean(); n=len(s)
    rho=float(np.corrcoef(s[1:],s[:-1])[0,1])
    rho=min(max(rho,-0.99),0.99)
    return n*(1-rho)/(1+rho), rho

mse=np.array([PO[k].mean() for k in KEYS])
w_lik=np.exp(-n_eff/2*np.log(mse/mse.min())); w_lik/=w_lik.sum()
for i,k in enumerate(KEYS):
    print('%-18s %8.4f %10.3f %12.3f %12.3f'%(k,rmse[k],w_ship[i],w_lik[i],w_lik[i]/w_ship[i]))
print('\nmax weight difference between the two weighting schemes: %.3f'%np.abs(w_lik-w_ship).max())
# effect on the scenario forecast
def scen(w):
    eta=np.zeros(9)
    for wi,k in zip(w,KEYS):
        X=F[k]; ok=np.isfinite(X[:NTR]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        m=sm.OLS(LG[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:NTR][idx]]).fit()
        eta=eta+wi*(np.c_[np.ones(9),X[NTR:]]@m.params)
    return 1/(1+np.exp(-eta))
ps,pl=scen(w_ship),scen(w_lik)
print('\nscenario q89: shipped weights %.4f | likelihood weights %.4f  (%+.1f%%)'%(
    ps[-1],pl[-1],100*(pl[-1]-ps[-1])/ps[-1]))
print('scenario q81: shipped weights %.4f | likelihood weights %.4f'%(

"""

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr); HOR=9
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if   k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
SPECS={
 'p1.5_logN':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'inv_logN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_cpi':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'inv_logN_cpi' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('cpi','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_gdp':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'inv_logN_gdp' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('gdp','log')],
 'p1.5_logN_du4':[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4')],
 'inv_logN_du4_u':[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','log'),('unemployment','d4'),('unemployment','log')],
 'inv_invN' :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'log_logN' :[('bbb_spread','log'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'logS'     :[('bbb_spread','log')],
}
F={k:build(v,CONC) for k,v in SPECS.items()}
KEYS=list(SPECS); ORIGINS=list(range(44,72))
def per_origin(k):
    X=F[k]; out=[]
    for T in ORIGINS:
        ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]],LG[idx],rcond=None)[0]
        out.append((np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]@b, LG[T:T+HOR]))
    return out
PO={k:per_origin(k) for k in KEYS}
def sqerr(k):
    return np.array([float(((pr-tr)**2).mean()) for pr,tr in PO[k]])
def eff_t(d):
    """t-statistic of mean(d) with an effective-n (AR1) correction"""
    d=np.asarray(d,float); n=len(d); s=d-d.mean()
    rho=float(np.corrcoef(s[1:],s[:-1])[0,1]); rho=min(max(rho,-0.99),0.99)
    n_eff=n*(1-rho)/(1+rho)
    se=s.std(ddof=1)/np.sqrt(n_eff)
    return d.mean()/se, n_eff, rho
print('=== effective-n corrected paired tests (per-origin mean squared error) ===')
pairs=[('p1.5_logN','inv_invN','log(nasdaq) vs reciprocal(nasdaq)'),
       ('p1.5_logN','logS','with nasdaq vs spread-only'),
       ('p1.5_logN','inv_logN','spread^-1.5 vs spread^-1'),
       ('p1.5_logN','log_logN','spread^-1.5 vs log(spread)')]
for a,b,lab in pairs:
    da=sqerr(a); db=sqerr(b)
    t,n_eff,rho=eff_t(da-db)
    naive=(da-db).mean()/(da-db).std(ddof=1)/np.sqrt(len(da))
    print('  %-36s t(naive)=%+.2f  t(eff-n, n_eff=%.1f, rho=%+.2f)=%+.2f  -> %s'%(
        lab,naive,n_eff,rho,t,'significant' if abs(t)>2 else 'NOT significant'))
print()
print('=== which weighting scheme generalises best? (9-quarter backtest) ===')
def backtest(scheme):
    P=[];Y=[]
    for T in range(48,72):
        mem=[];cvs=[]
        for k in KEYS:
            X=F[k]; ok=np.isfinite(X[:T]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
            m=sm.OLS(LG[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:T][idx]]).fit()
            Xd=np.c_[np.ones(HOR),X[T:T+HOR]]
            mem.append(Xd@m.params)
            cvs.append(float(np.sqrt(((Xd@m.params-LG[T:T+HOR])**2).mean())))
        cvs=np.array(cvs); cm=cvs.min()
        if scheme=='equal': w=np.ones(len(cvs))/len(cvs)
        elif scheme=='tau0.03': w=np.exp(-(cvs-cm)/0.03)
        elif scheme=='tau0.06': w=np.exp(-(cvs-cm)/0.06)
        elif scheme=='tau0.12': w=np.exp(-(cvs-cm)/0.12)
        elif scheme=='likelihood':
            mse=np.array([float(((mem[i]-LG[T:T+HOR])**2).mean()) for i in range(len(KEYS))])
            w=np.exp(-2.1/2*np.log(mse/mse.min()))
        w=w/w.sum()
        P.append(np.average(np.array(mem),axis=0,weights=w)); Y.append(LG[T:T+HOR])
    P=np.concatenate(P);Y=np.concatenate(Y)
    return np.sqrt(((P-Y)**2).mean()), np.mean(np.abs(1/(1+np.exp(-P))-1/(1+np.exp(-Y))))
for s in ['equal','tau0.12','tau0.06','tau0.03','likelihood']:
    r,m=backtest(s); print('   %-12s RMSE=%.4f  MAE(prob)=%.5f'%(s,r,m))

"""
================================================================================
 Stress loss model - quarterly portfolio default rate driven by macro factors
================================================================================
FINDINGS FROM THE DATA
----------------------
* Target  : log-odds logit(p) of the quarterly annualised default rate.  The
            rates are small fractions (0.0066 - 0.0632), so the log-odds link
            keeps forecasts in (0,1) and makes the modelling error additive -
            exactly what the prediction interval needs.
* Missing : bbb_spread starts at q8, vix at q16, hpi at q18, sp500/djia at q32.
            Every specification is fitted on the rows where the drivers IT uses
            are observed; nothing is imputed.
* Drivers : a search over all 2^9 driver subsets x a library of transforms
            (level / log / reciprocal / power / moving average / change),
            scored by 9-quarter-ahead expanding-window CV, always selects
            bbb_spread (strong, positive) and nasdaq (robust, negative).
            unemployment is 0.89 collinear with the credit spread and is NOT
            significant in a joint level fit - but its 4-quarter CHANGE is
            (t ~ 2.2), i.e. what matters is *sustained* deterioration.

"""
Decision-theoretic check: is the shipped point estimate close to loss-minimising?

The forecast is a mixture over hypotheses about the data-generating form.  Under
Gaussian log-odds noise the additive noise term is the same for every
hypothesis, so the loss-minimising point estimate is simply the posterior mean
of the hypothesis means.  This script:
  * computes the scenario conditional mean implied by each hypothesis,
  * weights the hypotheses by the evidence gathered (in-sample permutation
    significance for PRESENCE, effective-n paired tests for the FORM),
  * compares the expected loss of the shipped estimate against the
    loss-minimising one and against simple alternatives,
  * shows how sensitive the conclusion is to the posterior assumptions.
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('data/train.csv'); sc=pd.read_csv('data/scenario.csv')
LG=np.log(tr.default_rate.values/(1-tr.default_rate.values)); NTR=len(tr)
CONC=pd.concat([tr,sc],ignore_index=True)
def pw(s,p):
    s=np.asarray(s,float)
    return np.log(np.maximum(s,1e-9)) if p==0 else np.power(np.maximum(s,1e-9),p)
def build(spec,df):
    o=[]
    for c,k in spec:
        s=df[c].values.astype(float)
        if k=='d4': v=pd.Series(s).diff(4).values
        elif k=='log': v=pw(s,0.)
        elif k=='inv': v=pw(s,-1.)
        elif k=='p15': v=pw(s,-1.5)
        o.append(v)
    return np.column_stack(o)
HYP={
 'H1 log(nasdaq), saturating spread' :[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','log')],
 'H2 reciprocal(nasdaq)'              :[('bbb_spread','inv'),('nasdaq','inv')],
 'H3 no equity driver'                :[('bbb_spread','p15')],
 'H4 raw-level nasdaq'                :[('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','id')],
}
def hyp_mean(spec):
    X=build(spec,CONC); ok=np.isfinite(X[:NTR]).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
    m=sm.OLS(LG[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),X[:NTR][idx]]).fit()
    return np.c_[np.ones(9),X[NTR:]]@m.params
MU={k:hyp_mean(v) for k,v in HYP.items()}
# H4 needs a raw-level feature -> add it
X=build([('bbb_spread','p15'),('nasdaq','raw')],CONC) if False else None
def raw_nasdaq():
    A=np.column_stack([pw(tr.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), tr.nasdaq.values])
    ok=np.isfinite(A).all(axis=1); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
    m=sm.OLS(LG[idx],np.c_[np.ones(len(idx)),A[idx]]).fit()
    B=np.column_stack([pw(sc.bbb_spread.values,-1.5), sc.nasdaq.values])
    return np.c_[np.ones(9),B]@m.params
MU['H4 raw-level nasdaq']=raw_nasdaq()
sig=lambda a:1/(1+np.exp(-np.asarray(a)))
ship=np.log(pd.read_csv('predictions.csv').y_pred.values/(1-pd.read_csv('predictions.csv').y_pred.values))
print('hypothesis means at q89 (log-odds / probability):')
for k,v in MU.items(): print('   %-38s %+7.3f  ->  %.4f'%(k,v[-1],sig(v[-1])))
POST_PRIORS={
 'shipped CV weights (0.79/0.14/0.04/0.03)': (0.79,0.14,0.04,0.03),
 'evidence-balanced   (0.45/0.40/0.10/0.05)': (0.45,0.40,0.10,0.05),
 'form-tie            (0.45/0.45/0.10/0.00)': (0.45,0.45,0.10,0.00),
 'equity-doubtful     (0.40/0.15/0.40/0.05)': (0.40,0.15,0.40,0.05),
}
def loss(p_logit, post):
    """expected squared error in log-odds, averaged over the scenario quarters"""
    w=np.array(post); tot=0
    for wi,(k,v) in zip(w,MU.values()):
        tot+=wi*float(np.mean((p_logit-v)**2))
    return tot
def loss_prob(p_logit, post):
    w=np.array(post); tot=0
    for wi,(k,v) in zip(w,MU.values()):
        tot+=wi*float(np.mean((sig(p_logit)-sig(v))**2))
    return tot
print('\nexpected loss of candidate point estimates (mean over the 9 quarters):')
print('%-40s %12s %12s %10s'%('posterior / candidate','E[sq.err lg]','E[sq.err prob]','q89'))
for pname,post in POST_PRIORS.items():
    opt=np.average(np.array(list(MU.values())),axis=0,weights=np.array(post))
    cands={'loss-minimising (posterior mean)':opt,'SHIPPED ensemble':ship}
    for cname,pv in cands.items():
        print('%-40s %12.5f %12.6f %10.4f'%(pname+' | '+cname[:20],loss(pv,post),loss_prob(pv,post),sig(pv[-1])))
    print()
print('sensitivity of the loss-minimising q89 forecast to the posterior:')
for pname,post in POST_PRIORS.items():
    opt=np.average(np.array(list(MU.values())),axis=0,weights=np.array(post))
    print('   %-40s optimal q89=%.4f   shipped=%.4f   excess loss=%.5f'%(
        pname,sig(opt[-1]),sig(ship[-1]),loss(ship,post)-loss(opt,post)))
PYEOF
timeout 1200 python3 analysis/decision_loss.py
